decision:
Single Platform Node
Size based upon sizing document and best practices.
justification:
• Smallest footprint.
• Can be scaled-out to a platform cluster.
• Supports 10,000 virtual machines or objects.
implication:
• Requires a CPU and RAM reservation of 100% of the CPU and RAM assigned.
• No, high availability
• Requires the single node be deployed as an Extra Large size
subsection: VCF Operations for Networks - Scaling

decision:
Platform Cluster
• Three node clusters. Consisting of 3 platform instances. Can scale up to 15 XL nodes.
• Cluster node sizing starts at a Large Platform Node Size and go up to Extra Large.
justification:
• Highly Performant.
• Highly scalable.
implication:
• Cluster does not provide high availability. It is for performance.
• Requires higher CPU and memory reservations to support additional nodes.
subsection: VCF Operations for Networks - Scaling

decision:
Collector
A single VM used to monitor remote VCF deployments and to send data back to the primary cluster.
justification:
• Highly Performant.
• Highly scalable.
implication:
• Limitation of total flows is based on the capacity of the platform.
• Requires understanding the amount of VMs, Flows, and Edges will be sending data to the collector.
subsection: VCF Operations for Networks - Scaling

decision: Orchestrate cyber and ransomware recovery processes through an end-to-end automated workflow across infrastructure, network, and security tooling.
justification:
• End-to-end automated recovery workflows eliminate human error and manual handoffs during incident response.
• Significantly compresses operational downtime and minimizes the window during which business operations remain disrupted.
implication: Requires deploying unified recovery orchestration platforms capable of automating network quarantine and workload restoration.
subsection: Application Security and Recovery for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Restore workloads into an Isolated Recovery Environment (IRE) or Clean Room before re-introducing them into production.
justification:
• Restoring into an isolated recovery environment prevents compromised restore points from re-contaminating production networks.
• Restricts malware payload execution to a quarantined space.
• Minimizes the duration of operational risk during validation.
implication: Requires building an isolated recovery network boundary (cleanroom) with dedicated compute and network quarantine rules.
subsection: Application Security and Recovery for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Perform automated validation of restore point candidates in isolated cleanrooms using Next-Gen antivirus (NGAV) to detect fileless and file-based malware.
justification:
• Automated NGAV inspection on powered-on candidates identifies dormant malware and vulnerabilities before production failback.
• Reduces the risk and timeframe of re-introducing threats back into production.
implication: Requires integrating automated sandbox analysis and behavioral antivirus inspection into the cyber recovery pipeline.
subsection: Application Security and Recovery for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Standardize on a unified management platform for cyber recovery across infrastructure, networking, orchestration, and restore point validation.
justification:
• Consolidates recovery operations into a single management plane eliminates tool fragmentation and cross-team friction.
• Reduces RTO and minimizing the duration of business interruption during an incident.
implication: Requires consolidating legacy backup, replication, and disaster recovery tools into an integrated platform.
subsection: Application Security and Recovery for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Automate backup schedules to generate immutable, tamper-proof snapshots that resist deletion or modification by compromised administrative credentials.
justification:
• Cryptographically locked, immutable snapshots guarantee restore point integrity.
• Prevents ransomware or malicious administrators from wiping recovery data and minimizing the window of irrecoverable data loss.
implication: Requires enabling immutable cloud or air-gapped storage repositories with locked retention policies.
subsection: Application Security and Recovery for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Test and validate cyber recovery plans at least quarterly using automated execution workflows in isolated sandboxes.
justification:
• Regular non-disruptive testing ensures that operational playbooks stay aligned with application changes.
• Minimizes the time that is required to initiate recovery and preventing plan failures during live incidents.
implication:
• Requires adequate operational process to ensure that testing is prioritized to occur every 90 days.
• Demands scheduling non-disruptive, automated DR dry-runs in isolated sandboxes every 90 days.
subsection: Application Security and Recovery for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Automate workload compliance and vulnerability management across virtual machines and container workloads using desired-state enforcement and continuous CVE tracking.
justification:
• Guest-level vulnerability tracking and desired-state enforcement eliminate manual patching bottlenecks.
• Reduces the duration application-layer vulnerabilities and configuration drift remain exposed to exploitation.
implication: Requires deploying continuous workload compliance scanning and guest OS desired-state remediation tools.
subsection: Application Security and Recovery for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Establish and validate a recovery architecture capable of meeting an RTO measured in hours for critical systems following a cyber incident.
justification:
• Achieving an RTO of hours minimizes the total timeframe of business disruption, financial loss, and operational outage.
• A cyber attack or ransomware encryption event may result in destruction of data.
implication: Demands automated, live-mount instant recovery capabilities from immutable cloud storage to local hypervisor clusters.
subsection: Application Security and Recovery for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Assign a VNA cluster to the VPC Connection Profile. Select one of the presented Virtual Network Appliance Cluster Models.
justification: A VNA cluster is required for stateful network services when using a Distributed TGW with VXLAN integrations.
implication:
• Additional resources are required for the VNA cluster.
• Only traffic that is sourced from VPC private or private TGW subnets is forwarded to the VNA cluster to perform stateful services such as NAT.
subsection: Distributed VXLAN Connectivity Model for Version 9.1.1 with vSphere Supervisor or VCF-A All Apps Org Design Requirements

decision: Standardize infrastructure upgrade cycles on the latest available VCF software release.
justification:
• Running the latest software release proactively closes vulnerability exposure windows before automated exploit chains can proliferate.
• Fixes might originate from public security advisories or internally identified code improvements.
• Running older releases (N-1 or older) leaves known vulnerabilities that are exposed to automated scanning engines.
implication: Requires shortened qualification cycles, automated testing pipelines, and tight operational alignment with release cadences.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Perform general private cloud platform upgrades within a strict SLA that is measured in weeks.
justification: A multi-week operational upgrade window significantly shrinks the window of exposure, minimizing the time threat actors have to scan, identify, and exploit infrastructure vulnerabilities before updates are applied.
implication: Demands image-based lifecycle management and pre-authorized maintenance windows across workload domains to avoid application downtime.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Apply patches for VMSAs across the private cloud platform within a strict SLA that is measured in days.
justification:
Threat actors quickly analyze public VMSA disclosures to create exploit payloads.
Enforcing a multi-day patching SLA significantly compresses the exposure window and reduces the time VCF components remain vulnerable to targeted exploit attempts.
implication: Requires pre-staged patch pipelines, emergency change authorization pathways, and non-disruptive live patching capabilities.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Before deployment in production, complete qualification testing for general software upgrades within an SLA that is measured in days.
justification:
• Accelerating qualification testing to a multi-day SLA minimizes operational delay between patch availability and deployment.
• Reduces the duration of exposure during which known vulnerabilities could be exploited.
implication: Demands automated synthetic validation test suites and dedicated staging environments to replace manual regression testing bottlenecks.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Before deployment in productin, complete qualification testing for high-severity VMSAs within an emergency SLA that is measured in days.
justification:
• High-severity VMSAs represent prime targets for rapid exploitation.
• Establishes an expedited multi-day qualification window.
• Reduces the time critical vulnerabilities remain unverified for production.
• Allowing teams to authorize and roll out mitigations before threat actors can exploit the gap.
implication: Requires establishing dedicated, expedited qualification pathways specifically for VMSAs, independent of standard feature releases.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Adopt new platform security and operational capabilities upon General Availability (GA).
justification:
• Adopting new security releases promptly minimizes the duration during which the platform operates under legacy defense baselines.
• Reduces the time frame during which the infrastructure remains exposed to evolving threat vectors and security capability gaps.
implication: Operational teams must maintain continuous competency updates and agile architectural review boards to rapidly evaluate and validate new capabilities.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Standardize private cloud infrastructure on the VCF 9.1.x architecture.
justification:
• Upgrading to VCF 9.1.x provides native fleet-wide management, automated compliance drift remediation, and integrated security operations
• Reduces the window of time configuration gaps and legacy management silos remain exposed to potential threats.
implication: Might require architectural migration planning, hardware compatibility validation, and operational runbook updates.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Enforce guest operating system and application patch management protocols that can apply security updates within an SLA that are measured in days.
justification:
• Rapid guest OS and application patching significantly reduces the duration that known vulnerabilities remain accessible
• Reduces the window of opportunity for an initial workload compromise to be weaponized or escalated across the platform.
implication: Requires close operational alignment between infrastructure platform teams and application DevOps teams to automate guest OS patch delivery and testing pipelines.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Establish and maintain a dedicated, permanent internal Rapid Response Team for security incident management.
justification:
• Maintaining a permanent rapid response team ensures pre-coordinated incident protocols and active threat-hunting capabilities.
• Reduces time-to-detect and time-to-contain during security incidents.
• Reduces the duration that an active threat can operate within the environment.
implication: Requires dedicated headcount allocation, ongoing threat-hunting duties, and pre-authorized executive authority to execute emergency containment actions across the cloud fabric.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Enforce strict use of predefined protocol tasklists and incident runbooks during security events.
justification:
• Execution using standardized protocols minimizes decision latency and operational ambiguity during security events.
• Reduces the total duration that is required to contain active threats and limiting the potential window of disruption.
implication: Involves drafting detailed incident runbooks, performing regular dry-run simulation drills, and establishing automated containment triggers.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Align post-incident procedures with established compliance and security governance frameworks, such as ISO, NIST, SOC 2, or NERC.
justification:
• Standardized post-incident frameworks enforce structured root-cause remediation
• Reduces the time systemic vulnerabilities or architectural gaps remain in the environment to reduce the duration of exposure to recurring exploit attempts.
implication: Demands formal audit logging, rigorous forensic root-cause documentation, and executive and regulatory reporting mechanisms.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Perform regular third-party vulnerability assessments and penetration tests, sharing findings with security leadership and relevant stakeholders.
justification:
• Independent security assessments and penetration testing validate posture integrity.
• Minimizes the duration that undetected configuration drift, unpatched attack surface gaps, or legacy exposures remain present in the environment.
implication: Requires allocating recurring budget for third-party security services and establishing formal remediation tracking for identified findings.
subsection: Design Recommendations for People and Process for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Aggregate administrative and platform audit logs across the private cloud stack.
justification:
• Real-time log correlation connects API tokens directly to identity sessions, significantly reducing investigation latency.
• Minimizes the duration during which unauthorized API activity or compromised sessions remain undetected.
implication: Demands central log forwarding configuration with token-level session tracking and encrypted transport.
subsection: Design Recommendations for User Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Federate administrative identities by using a central identity plane with mandatory MFA and granular, job-specific role-based access control.
justification:
• Centralized federation with MFA and strict role-based access control reduces reliance on static credentials and restricts privilege boundaries.
• Minimizes the window of opportunity for credential misuse or unauthorized privilege escalation.
implication: Requires integrating VCF Single Sign-On with an enterprise identity provider, such as Okta, or Entra ID, and mapping granular VCF roles.
subsection: Design Recommendations for User Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Centrally automate and continuously monitor SSL/TLS certificate lifecycles across the fleet using enterprise certificate authority (CA) integration.
justification:
• Centralized, automated certificate lifecycle management maintains consistent cryptographic baselines.
• Reduces the duration that expired, misconfigured, or weak certificates create management plane exposure or unexpected outages.
implication: Shifts management from manual per-appliance scripts to centralized, automated CA renewal workflows that persist across platform updates.
subsection: Design Recommendations for User Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Centrally establish, continuously audit, and automatically enforce global password complexity, aging, and account lockout policies across all infrastructure systems.
justification:
• Centralized fleet-wide password policy enforcement eliminates configuration drift and local credential variations
• Minimizes the duration that non-compliant or weak authentication baselines remain exposed.
implication: Requires establishing automated password complexity, rotation, and lockout profiles across all infrastructure management components.
subsection: Design Recommendations for User Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Vault and automatically rotate high-privilege operating system, application, and service account credentials using native Privileged Access Management (PAM) integration.
justification:
• Dynamic PAM vaulting and continuous credential rotation compress the usable lifespan of secrets.
• Minimizes the duration that harvested or exposed service account credentials can be exploited for lateral movement.
implication: Requires integrating high-privilege service accounts, API clients, and OAuth tokens with an enterprise PAM solution.
subsection: Design Recommendations for User Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Standardize, continuously audit, and strictly enforce TLS 1.3/1.2 protocols and FIPS-validated cryptographic profiles across all management appliances.
justification:
• Enforcing modern TLS protocols and FIPS-validated cryptographic profiles eliminates legacy cipher support.
• Minimizes the window of opportunity for traffic interception, decryption, or man-in-the-middle attacks.
implication: Requires configuring fleet-wide TLS and FIPS enforcement profiles across all management appliances.
subsection: Design Recommendations for Platform Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Automate the deployment, continuous auditing, and remediation of security baselines aligned with VMware Security Configuration Guides (VCF SCG).
justification:
• Automated compliance drift detection and remediation significantly compress the duration configuration gaps exist
• Minimizes the timeframe during which VCF infrastructure components remain vulnerable to exploitation.
implication: Demands automated benchmark deployment and drift monitoring using central compliance toolchains.
subsection: Design Recommendations for Platform Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Require fleet-wide data-in-transit encryption across all live migrations (vMotion), fault tolerance streams, inter-host storage communication and storage replication.
justification:
• Enforcing mandatory transport encryption neutralizes unencrypted data exposure during live operations.
• Minimizes the duration active workload RAM and replication streams are susceptible to packet sniffing or memory extraction.
implication: Requires setting vMotion encryption to 'Required' globally and enabling host hardware acceleration.
subsection: Design Recommendations for Platform Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Mandate AES data-at-rest encryption across all storage datastores, integrated with enterprise Key Management Servers (KMS) and automated Key Encryption Key (KEK) rotation.
justification:
• Automated KEK rotation that is paired with datastore encryption reduces static cryptographic exposure.
• Minimizes the time window during which extracted storage snapshots or compromised physical media could expose underlying data.
implication: Requires integrating native vSAN / vSphere Encryption with an enterprise Key Management Server (KMS).
subsection: Design Recommendations for Platform Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Centralize proactive telemetry, security event correlation, and observability across the SDDC fabric using VCF Operations fleet management.
justification:
• Unified observability connects multi-layer security telemetry in real time.
• Reduces mean time to detect (MTTD) and minimizing the duration anomalous cross-stack behavior goes unnoticed.
implication: Requires centralizing telemetry and security event correlation across all SDDC management layers.
subsection: Design Recommendations for Platform Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Execute platform lifecycle updates and emergency security maintenance using Quick Patch, Reduced Downtime, and rebootless Live Patching capabilities.
justification:
• Rebootless patching and non-disruptive lifecycle workflows eliminate the operational friction of scheduled downtime.
• Reduces the exposure window between patch release and active host remediation.
implication:
• Requires a VCF release that supports Live Patching.
• Live Patching is not supported in conjunctions with some features.
subsection: Design Recommendations for Platform Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Enforce hardware-rooted trust across host infrastructure using UEFI Secure Boot integrated with automated TPM 2.0 remote attestation.
justification:
• Hardware attestation and Secure Boot protect hypervisor firmware integrity.
• Minimizes the time 'boot kit' modifications or unauthorized low-level kernel changes can persist without detection.
implication: Requires enabling UEFI Secure Boot on host hardware, installing TPM 2.0, and configuring vCenter remote attestation.
subsection: Design Recommendations for Platform Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Enforce multi-tenant compute, storage, and network isolation across tenant environments using VPCs and Supervisor Zones.
justification:
• Structural VPC isolation enforces strict hypervisor and network boundaries.
• Contains threat blast radius and minimizing the opportunity for a compromised tenant workload to pivot into adjacent tenant spaces.
implication: Requires implementing VPCs for VCF Automation and NSX multi-tenancy constructs to enforce strict logical boundaries.
subsection: Design Recommendations for Platform Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Automate compute isolation and workload placement policies using vSphere tags, VCF Automation Placement Policies, and tenant resource quotas.
justification:
• Automated placement policies and quotas ensure that high-security workloads execute on dedicated physical hosts.
• Minimizes the likelihood and duration of noisy-neighbor resource exhaustion or targeted Denial of Service (DoS) conditions.
implication: Demands configuring VCF Automation placement policies, vSphere tags, and explicit organization resource quotas.
subsection: Design Recommendations for Platform Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Automate continuous compliance enforcement and drift remediation using built-in security benchmarks that are paired with fleet-wide CVE visibility.
justification:
• Continuous benchmark tracking and integrated CVE insights replace periodic auditing cycles.
• Reduces the duration non-compliant states or unpatched vulnerabilities remain hidden across the fleet.
implication: Demands enabling VCF Security Posture Management with automated benchmark mapping and integrated CVE tracking across the fleet.
subsection: Design Recommendations for Platform Security for Defending Against Frontier AI Era Exploits

decision: Establish complete East-West traffic observability and flow monitoring across all VCF workload domains.
justification:
• Deep East-West traffic visibility uncovers hidden lateral movement patterns and unauthorized API probing.
• Minimizes the duration malicious reconnaissance or intra-VLAN threat propagation can occur undetected.
implication: Requires deploying distributed flow monitoring across all virtual switches and workload domains.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Enforce zero-trust micro-segmentation policies at the individual workload level (virtual machines, bare-metal hosts, and container pods).
justification:
• Workload-level ring-fencing restricts lateral connectivity.
• Reduces the blast radius of a compromised asset
• Minimizes the time and pathways that an attacker has to move horizontally across internal segments.
implication: Requires defining stateful micro-segmentation policies using distributed firewalling directly on host hypervisors.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Restrict and enforce stateful security controls on all communication between workloads and shared infrastructure services, such as DNS, NTP, Syslog, and Active Directory.
justification:
• Enforcing strict default-deny rules between workloads and shared services minimizes the exposure window for Active Directory abuse or service poisoning.
• Helps prevent compromised workloads from exploiting core infrastructure.
implication: Requires creating strict default-deny rules allowing only verified ports and protocols between workloads and core management services.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Isolate access to VCF management domains and infrastructure management interfaces by using dedicated micro-segmentation policies.
justification:
• Micro-segmenting management planes prevents compromised tenant workloads from probing or attacking SDDC infrastructure APIs.
• Minimizes the risk and duration of management plane exposure.
implication: Requires applying distributed firewall rules around management domain hosts, vCenter, and other VCF components.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Enforce simultaneous container security controls across both Kubernetes Pod and Node layers.
justification:
• Dual pod-and-node security limits the blast radius of container breakouts.
• Minimizes the opportunity and timeframe for an exploited pod to compromise underlying worker nodes or adjacent microservices.
implication: Requires integrating CNI-level micro-segmentation for Kubernetes container networks.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Aggregate and correlate network and host security alerts in real time using Network Detection & Response (NDR).
justification:
• Automated real-time event correlation stitches disparate network signals into threat campaigns.
• Reduces mean time to detect (MTTD) and minimizing alert fatigue for SOC teams.
implication: Demands deploying threat correlation engines capable of aggregating network traffic analysis and host alerts.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Deploy an Advanced Threat Prevention (ATP) suite—including Distributed IDS/IPS, Network Traffic Analysis (NTA), malware Prevention, and NDR—across all VCF workload clusters.
justification:
• Full-stack threat inspection detects polymorphic malware and zero-day exploit attempts in real time
• Minimizes the duration fileless execution or AI-driven command-and-control behavior can operate undetected.
implication: Requires activating distributed intrusion prevention, malware inspection, and traffic analysis across all cluster hosts.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Enforce and continuously audit regulatory compliance controls (PCI-DSS, HIPAA, FIPS, NERC) across East-West traffic flows.
justification:
• Continuous compliance enforcement ensures that sensitive data zones maintain audit-ready isolation.
• Reduces the duration non-compliant security postures or unmonitored traffic paths can persist.
implication: Requires mapping compliance benchmarks directly to distributed firewall and threat inspection rules.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Automate the creation, monitoring, and optimization of security policies via programmatic pipelines and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC).
justification:
• Programmatic policy automation ensures Zero Trust controls are applied instantly as workloads scale.
• Minimizes manual intervention delays and preventing security policy drift.
implication: Requires integrating firewall rule management into IaC pipelines, for example, Terraform or Ansible, and security automation platforms.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Continuously review, audit, and optimize firewall rule sets to eliminate redundant, shadow, or stale rules.
justification:
• Continuous rule optimization prevents policy bloat.
• Minimizes the timeframe over which overly permissive or obsolete firewall rules remain active in the environment.
implication: Requires implementing automated rule analysis tools to identify shadow rules and recommend cleanup.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Secure, load balance, and manage containerized application services using enterprise-grade Kubernetes API gateways.
justification:
• Software-defined ingress gateways deliver elastic traffic routing and TLS termination.
• Minimizes exposure to container ingress vulnerabilities and traffic overload attacks.
implication: Demands deploying software-defined load balancers tightly integrated with Kubernetes cluster control planes.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Protect external-facing applications using an active, analytics-driven WAF with zero-day virtual patching.
justification:
• Active WAF inspection and virtual patching compress the exposure window between the discovery of a vulnerability and the application code fixes.
• Blocks OWASP Top 10 threats in real time.
implication: Requires deploying central WAF policies with positive security models and signature-based threat detection.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats

decision: Automate SSL/TLS certificate lifecycles for applications to meet shortened certificate expiration requirements without manual intervention.
justification:
• Automated certificate renewal eliminates manual handling bottlenecks.
• Minimizes the risk and window of application outages that are caused by unexpected certificate expiration.
implication: Requires integrating load balancers and ingress gateways directly with enterprise CAs by using automated APIs.
subsection: Lateral Security for Securing VCF Against Frontier AI Era Threats
